work_order.confidence_rationale: All four findings were reproduced on this tree, the fix was implemented and measured in a real Chromium against the booted preview, and eight independent mutations were confirmed to fail the strengthened suite while the full suite stayed green. I re-measured the suite counts on this tree at 779a660: 297 pass / 0 fail across `node --test`, and 61 pass / 0 fail in test/web/pages.test.js. What is not measured is the /approvals card list, which the seeded preview cannot populate: no API path creates an approval.requested event, so that selector's coverage rests on the pinned declaration test and on the selector assertion rather than on a rendered page. The one judgement call left open - the exact wording of the assertion messages - is cosmetic.
work_order.understanding:
The ticket bundles four follow-ups to #48 (PR #65), and I reproduced all four on this tree before planning any of them. Three are weaknesses in the two tests #48 shipped in test/web/pages.test.js, both of which pass with a mutation that undoes the very fix they were written to pin; the fourth is a real layout defect QA measured and #48 explicitly declined to fix, which its own risks entry had already predicted. All four were re-verified as still open at 779a660; the tree is unchanged from the commit v1 was planned against. Finding 1 (test/web/pages.test.js:1305) - 'the narrow layout still carries the two declarations it depends on' reads the stylesheet with a non-global RegExp.prototype.exec and asserts on the first match only. Appending `#main > * { min-width: auto }` and `.table-scroll { overflow-x: visible }` to the end of src/web/styles.css leaves the suite at 61 pass / 0 fail, with both declarations the fix depends on overridden. Reproduced: same result, '# pass 61 # fail 0'. Finding 2 (test/web/pages.test.js:1347) - 'every table the five routes render is wrapped in a keyboard-reachable, named region' asserts wrappers.length === tables.length. That is satisfied equally by an empty `
` sitting next to a bare unwrapped ``. Reproduced by making tableRegion() in src/web/pages.js emit the region and the table as siblings: 61 pass / 0 fail, and the page now has an unscrollable table with no region at all - the exact keyboard contract AC-5 exists to protect. Finding 3 (test/web/pages.test.js:1349) - `wrappers.map((tag) => /\baria-label="([^"]*)"/.exec(tag)[1])` dereferences the match without checking it. Dropping the aria-label from the wrapper throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '1')` before any assertion runs, so the failure names neither the route nor the region, and the `assert.notEqual(label, '', ...)` on the following lines is unreachable for that case. Reproduced: 'not ok 60 ... name: TypeError'. The line below it, `for (const [tag, label] of wrappers.map((w, i) => [w, labels[where][i]]))`, re-derives the array it was just assigned from. Finding 4 (QA, pre-existing) - a long unbreakable name still scrolls the whole page sideways. I booted the preview on a temp DB, POSTed an experiment named with a 120-character unbreakable URL string and an opportunity with the same, and measured document.documentElement.scrollWidth over CDP at 320/375/414px. Matches QA: '/' and /experiments measure 581 at all three widths (QA: 572), /opportunities measures 587 (QA: 587). Culprits are LI.experiment-card, STRONG, SPAN on the two grid pages and STRONG on /opportunities - none of them inside a .table-scroll region. /approvals and /journal do not overflow today only because the seeded names are short. Nothing here turned out to have been fixed by a later round. All four hold.
work_order.root_cause: Two independent causes, one per half of the ticket. For the layout defect: #48 lifted the automatic minimum on #main's direct children (`#main > * { min-width: 0 }`, src/web/styles.css:135) but the floor on a grid item is one level down. `.experiment-list` and `.approval-list` are `display: grid` (src/web/styles.css:346-353), so their items keep the automatic minimum of min-content; a card whose widest child is a single unbreakable string sizes the track to that string. `.opportunity-list` is not a grid at all, so there the same string overflows an ordinary block child that refuses to break. No `overflow-wrap`, `word-break`, `hyphens` or `white-space` declaration exists anywhere in src/web/styles.css, and the markup is `${escapeHtml(name)}` inside the card (src/web/pages.js:461, 741, 813, 941), so the string is one unbreakable token. This is precisely the limit #48's own work order predicted ('overflow-wrap was deliberately NOT added ... a future unbreakable string wider than its container would still overflow its box'), and I measured that it is the whole of the remaining overflow. For the three test findings: the tests are anchored on the first match of a rule (finding 1) and on a count rather than a containment relation (finding 2), so both assert something weaker than the property their names claim. A declaration pinned by a first-match regex cannot see a later rule; a count cannot tell an empty region from a wrapping one. Finding 3 is a missing null check in the same three lines.
work_order.approach:
One stylesheet rule and four test edits, in the two files the ticket already names. Nothing is added, moved or refactored.

The fix is `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the three card lists and their descendants. I measured the alternatives in Chromium against the booted preview rather than choosing by memory, and the value is not interchangeable with the one a developer reaches for first:

- `overflow-wrap: break-word` on the cards: /experiments still measures 581 at 375px. It creates the break opportunity but leaves the intrinsic min-content width alone, so the grid track still sizes to the whole string. It fixes /opportunities only (587 -> 305), because that list is not a grid. This is the trap.
- `min-width: 0` on `.experiment-list > *` and `.approval-list > *`: /experiments still measures 564. Stopping the box from growing does not make the string break; the content still spills out of it.
- `word-break: break-all` on the cards: works, but breaks ordinary words mid-character as well as unbreakable ones. `anywhere` is the narrower instrument - it only adds break opportunities where there were none.
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` scoped to the three card lists and their descendants: /, /experiments and /opportunities all measure 305/360/399 at 320/375/414px, i.e. clientWidth, at every width, with the long fixtures in place.

A blanket `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `#main *` also clears the overflow, and I rejected it on measurement: it collapses every `.table-scroll` region from 755>278 on /journal and 620>278 on / to 278>278, because the table cells wrap to their column instead of scrolling in their own region. That is #48's fix undone by the cure, and the existing pinned test would not notice - it only checks that the declaration is present. The new rule must not name `.table-scroll`, `#main > *`, or any `td`/`th`.

Each of the three test findings is fixed at the strength the finding names, not by the cheaper option the reviewer offered as an alternative. Finding 1: the reviewer offered 'assert exactly one #main > * rule' as cheaper and equally effective. I am specifying the every-match form instead, because the count form is falsified by a legitimate future `@media` block re-declaring the same value, and because the every-match form is the one that states the actual property ('no rule anywhere in the file re-declares this to something else') and can distinguish a rule that declares the property twice. Finding 2: containment, as the reviewer specified. Finding 3: a named assertion on the match instead of a dereference, and a direct index instead of a re-derived second variable.

The overflow-wrap declaration is also pinned in a test, in the same style as the existing `.page-title` and #48 pinned tests, because the reviewer was right that the browser check is the only thing standing between this and a silent regression and that the browser check is not in CI. The pinned test is written in the every-match form from the start, so it does not carry the defect it is being added to fix.

I did not split the ticket. The three test findings and the layout defect all arise from the same PR, the two files are disjoint, and the four changes are small enough that splitting would buy two tickets' worth of review and CI for one line of CSS and three test edits. One coupling the implementer must know about: the new CSS rule must not use the `#main > *` or `.table-scroll` selectors, because the strengthened stylesheet test asserts on every rule matching those selectors and a second one now fails the suite.

Test counts after this change, since QA is given no memory of earlier runs and reads every number in this work order as a post-change expectation: test/web/pages.test.js goes 61 -> 62 (exactly one new test is added, and the other two tests are edited in place, not duplicated), and `node --test` across the repo goes 297 -> 298. Both were measured on this tree before the change: 61 and 297.

risks: The single change most likely to go wrong is the scope of the new rule. `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `#main *` clears the overflow just as well and is the shorter thing to write, but it also reaches the table cells: I measured every .table-scroll region collapsing from 755>278 to 278>278 on /journal and from 620>278 to 278>278 on /. The tables would wrap to their column, the regions would stop scrolling, and the existing pinned test would still pass because it only checks that the declaration is present - which is the blind spot this ticket exists to close. Scope the rule to the three card lists and their descendants, and do not name `.table-scroll`, `#main > *`, `td` or `th`.

The new CSS rule and the strengthened stylesheet test are coupled. The test now asserts on EVERY rule matching `#main > *` and `.table-scroll`, so adding the wrap by appending it to one of those rules - or by adding a second one - fails the suite. Add a new standalone rule, as specified.

`overflow-wrap: anywhere` differs from `break-word` in intrinsic sizing, not in line breaking, and only `anywhere` fixes the two grid-backed lists. Measured: break-word leaves /experiments at 581px, because it creates the break opportunity but the grid track is still floored at the string's min-content width. If a reviewer 'simplifies' this to break-word the overflow comes straight back, and the pinned test is what catches it.

`min-width: 0` on `.experiment-list > *` and `.approval-list > *` looks like the same fix and is not: measured, /experiments still measures 564px. A box that stops growing does not make its content break. Do not add it as part of this change.

overflow-wrap is a pinning test, not a layout test: it reads src/web/styles.css as text, in the deliberate style of the neighbouring `.page-title` and #48 pinned tests, because a stylesheet is not observable from a rendered page. It cannot tell you the page stops scrolling - only AC-1 through AC-3 and the QA script can, and they are not in CI. This is the limitation the review named, narrowed rather than closed; closing it entirely needs a browser check in CI, which is its own ticket (see out_of_scope).

The regexes in the pinned tests assume src/web/styles.css contains no `{` or `}` inside a comment. It does not today. A future comment carrying a brace would make the rule parser mis-segment the file and the pinned test would report a false failure, not a false pass. Acceptable for a pinning test; worth knowing before adding a commented-out rule.
No host is added and nothing leaves the machine: the change is a stylesheet rule and test assertions. Nothing in `env.api_allowlist` is implicated and no network call is introduced.
Nothing in `forbidden_paths` is touched, and nothing under .sdlc/memory/**, docs/** or .github/** is read or written by the implementation.
out_of_scope: A browser-driven layout check in CI. The review was right that the browser check is the only thing standing between a silent regression and a broken page and that it is not in CI. This ticket narrows the gap with a pinned test written in the every-match form, which is not the same as closing it. A headless-browser job asserting document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth at 320/375/414 is a separate ticket: it adds a browser dependency to a repo whose v1 has none, and 'no frontend build, no external services' is a project-level decision, not this ticket's to overturn.

Applying the wrap beyond the three card lists. The journal and approvals posture tables already sit inside a .table-scroll region and scroll; wrapping their cells would remove the need for the region rather than honour it. The nav, the tenant name and the checklist carry no user-supplied free text.

Changing the seeded fixtures to include a long unbreakable name, so the overflow would be reachable without POSTing one. That changes what every other ticket's QA sees on a seeded preview. The QA script POSTs its own fixture instead, against a temp DB_PATH.

`word-break: break-all` as the wrap value. It also fixes the overflow (measured), but it breaks ordinary words mid-character as well as unbreakable ones, which is a visible change to how every card reads. `anywhere` adds break opportunities only where there were none.

`min-width: 0` on `.experiment-list > *` and `.approval-list > *`. Measured to be neither sufficient nor necessary for this defect (564px, still over). If a future ticket widens some other unbreakable content, it may be worth adding on its own evidence.

A named utility class or a shared `.card` base for the three card lists. The duplication predates this ticket and collapsing it is a refactor with its own regression surface; the fix does not need it.

The /approvals card list is fixed by the same selector but cannot be exercised on a seeded preview - no API path creates an approval.requested event, so the pending queue is always empty in the preview. It is covered by the pinned test's selector assertion, not by a rendered page. A fixture or a preview override for a pending approval is its own ticket.

alternatives_considered.approach: Assert the stylesheet contains exactly one `#main > *` rule and exactly one `.table-scroll` rule - the cheaper fix the reviewer offered as equally effective.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is falsified by a legitimate future `@media` block re-declaring the same value, and it only detects a second rule - not a rule that declares the property twice, or a change to the property inside the existing rule. The every-match form states the property that actually matters (no rule anywhere re-declares it to a conflicting value) and is no harder to read. Implemented and mutation-tested: it fails on an appended override, on a flipped value in the existing rule, and on a rule that declares the property twice.

That is #48's shipped fix undone by the cure, and the existing pinned test cannot see it - which is precisely finding 1. The rule must be scoped to the three card lists.

The three review findings are still open. Verified individually on this tree at 779a660 by applying each mutation and observing the suite stay at 61 pass / 0 fail; the same three mutations all fail the suite as specified here.

The QA finding is pre-existing and not introduced by #48. Confirmed by reading: #48 added only `#main > * { min-width: 0 }` and `.table-scroll { overflow-x: auto }`, and src/web/styles.css contains no overflow-wrap, word-break or hyphens declaration anywhere, before or after.

The pre-change suite counts are 297 across `node --test` and 61 in test/web/pages.test.js, both measured on this tree at 779a660 after `npm ci`. Every count in this work order is the post-change figure, and the two differ by exactly the one new test the plan adds.
unknowns: /approvals could not be measured with a real long name: the seeded preview's pending queue is empty and no API path creates an approval.requested event, so the .approval-card path is covered by the pinned test's selector assertion and by the fact that .approval-list is a display:grid with the same shape as .experiment-list, not by a rendered page. A ticket that adds a pending-approval fixture should confirm it.

Whether the .table-scroll regex in the pinned test would be confused by a media query that re-declares the property. It would not fail - a matching rule inside @media is collected by the same regex and required to declare the same value, which is the correct outcome - but I did not construct that case, and the count-based alternative the reviewer proposed would have failed it.
residual_risks: The pinning tests read src/web/styles.css as text with regexes. They cannot see a defect that is correct in the stylesheet and wrong in the layout - a cascade interaction, a specificity conflict with a later rule the regex does not match, a browser-specific wrap. That gap is narrowed (an appended override is now caught) but not closed, and closing it needs a browser check in CI, which is out of scope here.

The every-match assertions require each matching rule to declare the property exactly once with the required value. A future legitimate need - a second `#main > *` rule in a `@media (min-width: 900px)` block that also says `min-width: 0` - passes, but one that adds a different property to the same rule's body passes too only if it does not re-declare min-width or overflow-x. That is the intended strictness, and the assertion message names the rule index and the values it found, so a false failure is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

Evidence: Fresh DB (/tmp/qa67b.db) seeded, then one `approval.requested` envelope appended through the repository layer with name 'Raise budget' - 11 characters, no long token. With the PR's stylesheet: document.documentElement.scrollWidth is 463 at viewport widths 320, 375 AND 414 (overflow at all three; not present at 768). Ancestor-aware sweep, excluding .table-scroll, names LI.approval-card, STRONG, SPAN, FORM.approval-actions, BUTTON.button.button-secondary. Child widths of the flex row: LABEL:1, INPUT:234, BUTTON:63, BUTTON:60; computed flex-wrap is 'nowrap'. Same measurement with origin/main's styles.css: scrollWidth 546, so the new rule reduces 546 -> 463 and does not reach zero. On the long-named fixture it is 463 as well. Nothing else on /approvals spills: the only other .table-scroll region reads 319>293, i.e. it still scrolls. Note: NO acceptance criterion covers this. AC-1 names only /, /experiments and /opportunities, and qa_script step 9 checks /approvals 'with only the seeded fixtures' - which renders no card at all, so it passes vacuously. The finding is that the work order's out_of_scope entry ('The /approvals card list is fixed by the same selector') is false, and the new pinned test's `.approval-card` assertion at test/web/pages.test.js:1349-1352 certifies a route the fix does not fix. It is latent, not live: grep for 'approval.requested' across src/ and scripts/ returns exactly one hit, the read at src/web/pages.js:913, so no code path creates one and the queue is always empty in a running preview. That is why no seeded QA run could see it - I had to append the envelope through the repository layer to reach the route.

Concretely: the actions row needs `min-width: 0` on the input plus `flex-wrap: wrap` (or `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0` on the input) so the row can shrink - `overflow-wrap` cannot do this job, and adding it to `.approval-card *` does not help. `test/web/pages.test.js:1350`

Evidence: Mutation: change `.opportunity-row` to `.opportunity-roww` at src/web/styles.css:386 and :389 (both the bare and the `*` form). Result: `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` -> 62 pass / 0 fail, the pinned test green. Layout in Chromium at 320/375/414: /opportunities document.documentElement.scrollWidth 469 against innerWidth 320/375/414 - AC-1 regresses at all three widths, ancestor sweep names STRONG (the same culprit and the same 469 measured on the pre-fix baseline). Cause: `wrapping.some(([, selector]) => selector.includes('.' + cls))` is a substring test, so `.opportunity-roww`, `.opportunity-row-old` and `.opportunity-row:hover` all satisfy `includes('.opportunity-row')`. The same weakness admits a class named only in prose: the `([^{}]+)` group at test/web/pages.test.js:1344 swallows the 22-line CSS comment at src/web/styles.css:364-383 into the 'selector', so a comment mentioning the class satisfies the assertion with no selector doing so. Two further mutations, both uncaught by the suite: dropping the bare `.opportunity-row` from the group while keeping `.opportunity-row *` -> 62 pass; dropping the bare `.experiment-card` the same way -> 62 pass. Those two happen to be harmless in layout (measured: /experiments still 375=375 at 375px, because `overflow-wrap` is inherited and the descendant's soft-wrap opportunities still count toward the ancestor's min-content), so the suite's silence there is correct by luck rather than by design. Only removing a class from the selector entirely is caught (M4b: 'the overflow-wrap rule covers .opportunity-row' fails). I checked the adjacent false-failure direction and it is clean: prose containing `#main > * { min-width: 0 }` or `overflow-wrap: normal` inside the new comment leaves the suite at 62 pass, so the parser does not mis-segment on the comment this PR added.

Fix: Stop asserting on a substring of the rule text. Split the selector on commas, drop the leading comment, split each compound on whitespace, and require that some compound's leading simple selector is exactly `.<cls>` (or `.<cls>` followed only by combinators/pseudo-classes) - that at least catches `.opportunity-roww` and a class named only in prose. Better, assert against something observable: the rendered HTML for /experiments, /opportunities and /approvals already contains `class="experiment-card"`, `class="opportunity-row"` and `class="approval-card"` (src/web/pages.js:461, 741, 813, 941), so the pinning test can require that the rule's class list and the markup's class list are the same three names. That closes the gap a stylesheet-text test cannot: a selector that matches nothing in the page the server actually renders.
